newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: At least 50 hurt in Bangladesh strike violence.
newsitem.headline: At least 50 hurt in Bangladesh strike violence.

text.p: At least 50 people were wounded in bomb blasts and other violence during an eight-hour countrywide strike called by opposition Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP) on Sunday, police and witnesses said.
They said 15 people were hurt when the engine and a passenger coach of a train ran off tracks that had been damaged by unknown attackers at Hasimpur, 32 km (20 miles) from the port of Chittagong.
Five others were injured in bomb explosions in the city, where police arrested at least 10 BNP pickets, witnesses said.

In Dhaka, former home (interior) minister Abdul Matin Chowdhury, leading a group of pickets, was hit by a stone while passing by offices of the ruling Awami League. He was taken to hospital bleeding from the head, witnesses said.
BNP sources said Chowdhury was beaten by police.
The strike, called by the BNP of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, shut businesses and kept transport off the roads.
Strike enforcers, many carrying sticks and wearing headbands, marched on the streets of Dhaka, and set off dozens of home-made bombs and firecrackers, witnesses said.
They said strike supporters and opponents fought running battles in Dhaka's Mirpur area, where nearly 10 people were injured.
Riot police and para-military forces patrolled streets and guarded key installations as the strike virtually halted life across Bangladesh, witnesses said.
Officials in Chittagong said the strike shut everything including the port. The coutry's two bourses in Dhaka and Chittagong were also closed.
Other main cities including Khulna, Rajshahi, Sylhet, Netrokona and Mymensingh also witnessed strike-related violence which wounded some 20 people, local reporters said.
Rail and air traffic operated but with fewer passengers, transport officials said.
In Dhaka, hundred of government employees either walked to their offices or took pedal rickshaws, which operated in defiance of the strike. Many senior officials stayed in their offices overnight.
The BNP called the stoppage for Sunday, a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh, in its first major attempt to destabilise the eight-month-old government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

Hasina took office last June after defeating the BNP in a general election in which both the BNP and Hasina's Awami League accused each other of vote-rigging, but which was billed as free and fair by local and international monitors.

The BNP says the strike is to protest what it views as the government's failure to provide the basic needs of people in this poor nation and against Hasina's warmer ties with rival India, which the BNP sees as a plot to surrender Bangladeshi sovereignty.
